title: Signal school: trains as a radio teletype operator
description: In 1964 Larry completed a 15-week Army Signal school course as a radio teletype operator, the specialty his DD-214 lists for him. He remembers the school as Fort Gordon, Georgia, just outside Augusta, where he went after basic training at Fort Ord, California. It is the training behind the radio work he describes on the mountain and in the radio van.
researchNotes: 2026-09-14: corrected from 17 to 15 weeks. The 2026-08-10 transcription of the family photograph of the DD-214 read the course as 17 weeks and the MOS as 054.20; the clear scan of 2026-08-15 reads "SIG … 15 WKS 64 … RAD TT OPN" (item 25) and MOS 05C20, RAD TT OPER (item 23a) (research/records-request/dd214-findings.md, "Clear-scan corrections"). The badge (confirmed) rates the course and specialty, which the form documents. The location is his, not the form's: "then to fort Gordon or Eisenhower now in Georgia for radio school. It's right outside of Augusta Georgia" (giscus-vn-0024-c18119890, 2026-08-22, transcribed), with basic training "in Port Ord in Monterey Bay California" in the same comment. That retired the earlier Fort Gordon / Fort Benning question; Fort Benning is the separate place he remembers volunteering for Vietnam (1964-fort-benning-volunteer).
